links.outcome: Critical errors in GPT-4 responses to mild TBI cases, as identified by emergency physicians
links.effect: Responses containing critical errors had significantly lower satisfaction and scientific adequacy (p < 0.001). Ease of understanding did not differ between responses with and without critical errors (p = 0.133).
links.quote: However, responses with critical errors significantly reduced satisfaction and scientific adequacy (p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Readability of GPT-4 responses (Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level) versus case descriptions
links.effect: GPT-4 responses were significantly more difficult to read than the case descriptions (p < 0.001).
links.quote: GPT-4 responses were significantly more difficult to read than the case descriptions (p < 0.001).

screen.reason: Evaluates the performance and safety (critical errors and readability) of GPT-4 across clinical vignettes of mild traumatic brain injury without testing a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
